facts.text: JSBGym provides reinforcement learning environments for the control of fixed-wing aircraft using the JSBSim flight dynamics model and implements the Gymnasium interface
The documented use is gym.make(ENV_ID), then env.reset() and env.step(action), which returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info
The FlightGear-disabled Cessna 172 HeadingControlTask environment is registered as C172-HeadingControlTask-Shaping.STANDARD-NoFG-v0
The observation is an 11-tuple: altitude, pitch, roll, body velocities u, v, w, body rates p, q, r, altitude error and track error
Actions are 3-tuples of floats in the range [-1, +1] describing the aileron, elevator and rudder commands
The state space is a Box built from each state variable's min and max with dtype float64
The action space is a Box built from each action variable's min and max with dtype float64
The HeadingControlTask action variables are the aileron, elevator and rudder commands
The altitude bound is -1400 to 85000 ft, the pitch bound is -pi/2 to pi/2 and the roll bound is -pi to pi
The body-frame velocity bounds u, v and w are -2200 to 2200 ft/s
The body-rate bounds p, q and r are -2*pi to 2*pi rad/s
The aileron, elevator and rudder command bounds are -1.0 to 1.0
The task's nine base state variables are altitude, pitch, roll, u, v, w, p, q and r
The HeadingControlTask state adds the altitude error and the track error to the nine base variables
The altitude error is bounded by the altitude bounds and the track error is bounded -180 to 180 deg
The initial altitude is 5000 ft
The initial heading is 270 deg
The default episode time is 60 s
The default agent interaction frequency is 5 Hz
The episode step budget is ceil(episode_time_s * step_frequency_hz) agent steps and steps_left is bounded 0 to that budget

Each task step decrements steps_left and the task terminates when steps_left is zero or less, the last assessment reward is below MIN_STATE_QUALITY, or the altitude error exceeds MAX_ALTITUDE_DEVIATION_FT
MIN_STATE_QUALITY is 0.0 and MAX_ALTITUDE_DEVIATION_FT is 1000 ft
JSBSim integrates at 60 Hz and the environment runs JSBSIM_DT_HZ // agent_interaction_freq integration steps per agent step
The environment rejects an agent interaction frequency above JSBSIM_DT_HZ
The environment constructs the task with the agent interaction frequency and then takes the observation and action spaces from the task
step() calls the task for sim_steps_per_agent_step integration steps and returns observation, reward, terminated, False and info
reset(seed, options) seeds the environment, reinitialises or creates the simulation and returns the first observation and an info dict
NoFGJsbSimEnv is the training variant: it constructs the simulation with allow_flightgear_output=False
The package registers every aircraft/task/shaping setting and uses NoFGJsbSimEnv as the entry point when FlightGear is disabled
Environment ids are built as aircraft-task-shaping-FG or NoFG-v0
The simulation constructs an in-process jsbsim.FGFDMExec and sets sim_dt to 1/sim_frequency_hz

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 selects the seed the next reset records; the default HeadingControlTask initial conditions are fixed and the fake's transition is deterministic, so the same actions repeat the same trajectory.  The seed does not reproduce a JSBSim run: the fake backend is a separate kinematic stand-in and was not compared with JSBSim.

gaps: the fake backend is a hand-written kinematic stand-in, not JSBSim: no aerodynamic forces, no flight-dynamics integration, no contacts and no actuator, sensor or noise model; the upstream jsbsim.FGFDMExec is never executed, so fidelity level F0 is claimed for what this package deploys
the observation is an 11-number Python list from the stand-in's own equations, not the JSBSim outputs listed in facts.md, and it was never compared with a JSBSim run
the reward is a placeholder function of the stand-in's altitude and track errors; the upstream assessors and potential-based shaping rewards are not reproduced
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only; JSBSim has an optional set_simulation_time_factor (simulation.py:209-224) that the fake does not implement
timestep_ms 200 is the agent interaction interval: 12 integration steps of 1/60 s each, not the 16.67 ms integration step itself
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the seed is accepted and recorded, but the default HeadingControlTask initial conditions are fixed, so the seed alone does not change the first observation
the fake has no rendering, no FlightGear output and none of the upstream visualisers

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: step, reset and seed are refused after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation stays readable
